title: Proof-of-Agentness: Towards Verifying Agents on the Web
abstract: arXiv:2610.35288v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: CAPTCHAs and bot detection have helped protect Web services from automated abuse for decades by distinguishing humans from bots. However, the emergence of LLM-powered agents introduces a new setting: Web services increasingly accommodate agents as legitimate users. Without a way to distinguish agents from other automated clients such as simple bots and scripts, these services risk large-scale automated junk submissions that waste service resources and consume users' attention or tokens. In this paper, we investigate a novel question for today's Web: "How can a Web service obtain evidence that a client is an agent?" We introduce the concept of "Proof-of-Agentness" (PoA), a mechanism for distinguishing agents from other automated clients, motivated by the parallel between human attention and an agent's inference resources. We outline two approaches: active verification through challenge-response and passive analysis of service-visible sign

translated_title: 智能体证明：迈向Web上的智能体验证
translated_abstract: 验证码（CAPTCHA）和机器人检测几十年来一直通过区分人类与机器人来保护Web服务免受自动化滥用。然而，由大语言模型（LLM）驱动的智能体的出现带来了新的情境：Web服务日益将智能体接纳为合法用户。如果无法将智能体与简单机器人和脚本等其他自动化客户端区分开来，这些服务将面临大规模自动化垃圾提交的风险，从而浪费服务资源，并消耗用户的注意力或令牌。在本文中，我们针对当今的Web研究了一个新问题：“Web服务如何获得客户端是智能体的证据？”我们提出了“智能体证明”的概念，这是一种将智能体与其他自动化客户端区分开来的机制，其动机源于人类注意力与智能体推理资源之间的相似性。我们概述了两种方法：通过挑战-响应机制进行主动验证，以及对服务可见信号进行被动分析……
tldr: 本文提出了“智能体证明”这一新概念，使Web服务能够将LLM驱动的智能体与简单机器人和脚本等其他自动化客户端区分开来，从而防止大规模自动化垃圾提交对服务资源和用户注意力的滥用。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "Proof-of-Agentness" (PoA), a novel mechanism enabling Web services to distinguish LLM-powered agents from other automated clients such as simple bots and scripts, thereby protecting services from large-scale automated junk submissions.
